newsitem.title: USA: Brady bonds stagnate as market waits for Fed.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds stagnate as market waits for Fed.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices barely moved Friday as Brady bond traders wiled away the hours in anticipation of the Federal Reserve's policy meeting on Tuesday, traders said.
"Nothing happened today," one Brady trader said. "Today was a day to stay home. We're just waiting for Tuesday."

The bond markets expected the Fed to raise U.S. short-term interest rates by 25 basis points at the meeting, although a strong minority of U.S. economists figured the U.S. central bank would leave rates steady during a presidential electoral season amid scant indications of inflation.
Friday Brady bond trade was moribund as the only activity seemed confined to Wall Street dealers pushing prices around.
"It's clear that customers were not doing much of anything all day long" said another Brady bond trader.
Emerging market dealers seemed more concerned with the state of their golf games that the state of the market, one analyst said.
"It's goign to be like this until the FOMC," said Peter Allen, Bank of Boston's director of research "The Treasury market is the key right now."
The more liquid Bradies slipped slighty with Argentine FRBs ARFLC05=RR edged down 3/8 to 82-1/8 and Brazilian C bonds BR8D14=RR dipped 1/4 to 68-1/2.
But Mexican Pars MX625L19=RR and Argentine Pars AR4C23=RR were unchanged at 68-5/8 and 56-5/8.

"I would be very surprised if anything happens until this Fed meeting," said Brian Barish, head of emerging market research at Lazard Freres. "I don't think we're going to get any news that could cause a breakout either up or down in the Brady market for some time."
